newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Saflife paid 2.47 bln rand for JCI stake - paper.
newsitem.headline: Saflife paid 2.47 bln rand for JCI stake - paper.

text.p: Financial services group Saflife on Monday paid Anglo American Corp of South Africa 2.47 billion rand for a 30 percent stake in mining house JCI, a local newspaper quoted Saflife chairman Larry Nestadt as saying.
The paper said on Tuesday that Saflife's listing had been transferred from the Johannesburg Stock Exchange insurance sector to the mining financial/mining houses sector.
JCI spokesman Marc Gonsalves said JCI chairman Mzi Khumalo would announce the new JCI board once the Saflife consortium had finalised appointments.

Saflife announced in early April it planned to raise 2.25 billion rand via a rights offer and 154.6 million rand by way of an offer of warrants to finance black empowerment consortium African Mining Group's purchase of a controlling stake in JCI.
